lesson.title: Solving Quadratic Equations
intro: Quadratic equations can often be solved by moving all terms to one side and factoring or rewriting the equation.
Some quadratic equations can be solved by recognizing equivalent forms, such as completed-square form.
A quadratic equation may have two solutions, one solution, or no real solutions.
Always check which answer choice matches the full solution set.

steps: Look for two numbers that multiply to \(-16\) and add to \(6\).
Set each factor equal to zero: \(x=-8\) or \(x=2\).
workedExample.aiHint: Try factoring first, and remember the zero-product property.

questions.prompt: What is the solution set to the equation \(3x^2=24x\)?
questions.explanation: Rewrite as \(3x^2-24x=0\), then factor: \(3x(x-8)=0\). So the solutions are \(x=0\) and \(x=8\).

questions.prompt: Which equation has the same solutions as \(x^2+6x-18=0\)?

questions.explanation: To complete the square, add \(9\) to both sides: \(x^2-6x+9=27+9\). So \((x-3)^2=27+9\).
